Copyright (c) 1998-2025. Full license: crates/giggles-pg-types/tests/fixtures/POSTGRESQL-COPYRIGHT.
Source/hash/image/version/API/fixture counts: manifest.json. Source retained numeric.c.
Adapted numeric_power, power_var, power_var_int; reused ln_var and exp_var adaptation.
Power integer path uses rounded repeated squaring with REL18 variable precision,
not generic exp(ln(x)*y). Fractional and large integer path uses REL18 two-pass
ln scale selection, independent final power scale and guarded exp computation.
Floating point used only for source scale/range estimates; result digits BigInt.
The shared Decimal exp refactor preserves checked_exp scale policy.
Full decimal parse supplies REL18 double estimates, avoiding truncated-leading-digit estimates.

Generator generate.py captures SQL oracle.sql; actual PG18 network-none tmpfs owned
oracle. Durable fixture columns op|base/input|exponent/value|text|dscale|binary hex.
ERROR rows preserve actual SQLSTATE; API maps these domain/overflow errors to Range.
NaN/infinity/zero/negative-base precedence, int32 edges and large integral parity,
fixed-seed random cases, modular samples, near-one cancellation to16000 places,
scale1000 caps, huge/tiny ln/log and exp underflow boundaries included.
Properties are supporting samples, not proofs of last-digit rounding.
Representation ceiling stays MAX_DIGITS16384/MAX_SCALE16383, narrower than PG.
One oracle result exceeds coefficient ceiling and explicitly expects Limit.
Integer intermediates have explicit pre-multiplication bit budgets and significant
digit bound: Limit can occur even where a PostgreSQL result is representable.
Scratch decimal powers retain60000 bound derived from input/guard scales; no
iteration cap silently returns approximations. Source guard-digit algorithms
reproduce PostgreSQL behavior, not a universal correctly-rounded theorem.
No deps/locks/old arithmetic/float/temporal/core/harness modifications.
